title: Bridging Cultural Distance Between Models Default and Local Classroom Demands: How Global Teachers Adopt GenAI to Support Everyday Teaching Practices

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 30 K-12 teachers from South Africa, Taiwan, and the US to evaluate the 'cultural distance' between GenAI default repertoires (often US-centric) and local classroom demands, including indigenous knowledge and culturally relevant activities.

Evaluating teacher accounts from interviews regarding the models' inability to accurately process, generate, or support low-resource and indigenous languages (such as Sepedi and Afrikaans) compared to high-resource languages like English.

Examining qualitative reports from teachers about policy-level controls and built-in product censorship, such as models from Mainland China blocking politically sensitive queries regarding Taiwan, or US-based models reflecting local state-level bans.
